questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I decided to study abroad for various reasons, but the biggest one was to improve my second language, make international friends, and open up new academic possibilities. I wanted to be in a diverse environment that would help me connect with people from around the world. I looked for top-notch schools with specialized programs and resources to support my academic growth. It was also important for me to have opportunities for post-study work and internships to gain practical experience. My goal was to have an amazing and enriching experience that would help me grow personally, professionally, and culturally.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, but I am glad that I came here with my friend so we could help each other out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I don't recall getting any assistance when arriving

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the things you must do before, during, and after the exchange is very confusing and it takes up a lot of time and energy.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found it difficult. The student accommodation site was confusing and it seemed that everything was taken.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive but it also has its advantages.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I asked other exchange students, where to go and then it was all fine. There is just a lot to do and find out at the beginning of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a student adviser I could ask for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was fine. I tried to change one of my courses, but all the other courses I wished for, were unfortunately fully booked.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to fellow exchange students or maybe friends who already have been on exchange

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I went on an undergraduate programe

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is different but also fun to try something a lot different. It is more active participation and the best difference was that they put in a lot of work to give a lot of feedback on assignments.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Working and relating: developing your people skills
Language and Communication in Health and Society
Innovation and healthcare

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Working and relating: developing your people skills
The teachers were great and I had a big learning outcome, which I can use in my future studies

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: In order to get the full experience I think it is important to travel around in the country you study in. Therefore traveling and small trips were an unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing is extremely expensive in Edinburgh.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Edinburgh provides a lot of sport and other societies you can join

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds. You could choose between 90 different societies, for a small amount of money. And I also joined the student gym, where they also provide a lot of different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would defiantly recommend people to join some of the societies and the gym

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Buy tickets for the day trips even though it is expensive. It is absolutely worth it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was fine.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Agin join the societies and also the events Erasmus is hosting. That was how I met all of my friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The slow living, I feel like everyone here is never in a rush which is nice. I also love that most of the people in Edinburgh are students and it just gives a nice vibe.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go to the Erasmus events in the beginning in order to meet other exchange students. 
Be open-minded when meeting people from all over the world. 
Say yes to all the opportunities that come across. Time flies on exchange so you better get the most out of it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are unsure of your courses use time on exploring other courses and maybe go to other courses in the beginning and then reach out to your contact person in Edinburgh

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving English. Getting friends from all over the world. And getting to have another home in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: For me, it was that even though I got a lot of new sweet friends, it isn't as many as I have at home so I had a lot of time alone. But I learned to enjoy the alone time which is also another rewarding thing about exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
